html:
The Kayapó, who call themselves Mebêngôkre, "people of the water's source", are a Gê speaking people of the Xingu basin in southern Pará and northern Mato Grosso, Brazil.

They live in large round villages around a central plaza, grow sweet potatoes, manioc and maize, and hunt and fish across a huge forest territory. They are known for body paint, feather headdresses and the lip plates once worn by leading men. They often fought their neighbours, such as the Tapirapé and the Panará, and resisted settlers into the 1900s.

Since the 1980s the Kayapó have been among the best known Indigenous peoples in the world. Their leader Raoni Metuktire toured with the singer Sting to win support. In 1989 a Kayapó gathering at Altamira helped stop plans for dams on the Xingu, though the Belo Monte Dam was later built. Their demarcated lands now protect a large block of rainforest from loggers and gold miners.
